hints.title: Overtaking Restriction
hints.text: A faster car cannot pass a slower car ahead of it. How can sorting cars by initial position simplify the arrival order?

hints.title: Arrival Time Monotonicity
hints.text: If a car starts behind another car and reaches the target in less or equal time, it catches up and merges into that car's fleet before or at the target.

hints.title: Backward Pass Fleet Tracking
hints.text: Pair each car position with speed and sort descending by position. Calculate time to target as (target - position) / speed. If the current car takes strictly more time than the leading fleet ahead, it forms a new fleet and becomes the new lead time. Count total fleets formed.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Sorting cars takes O(N log N) time, followed by an O(N) backward pass.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating time step by step requires discrete time increments that fail with fractional catch-up times or large target distances (target up to 10^6).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting by initial position in O(N log N) time and O(N) space allows determining fleet formation in a single backward pass without step-by-step physics simulation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Understanding that sorting descending by position eliminates overtaking ambiguity, using floating-point time calculations accurately, and collapsing fleets without simulating time steps.
